# The core four, mapped to polytropos

!!! note
    Mirrored from `docs/sdd/core-four.md` — edit the source, then run `python3 bin/docs_build.py build`.

!!! tip "Standalone page"
    The standalone HTML version of this page is [core-four.html](core-four.html).

**Spec Kit's Specify → Plan → Tasks → Implement, and the polytropos file or command that does
each job.**

GitHub's Spec Kit names the spec-driven development loop as four core phases: **Specify** (what
and why, with no technology choices), **Plan** (the technical approach), **Tasks** (the plan cut
into ordered, checkable work items), and **Implement** (executing those items). A project
**constitution** sits above all four. Clarification and consistency checks sit between them:
in Spec Kit's methodology document as `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers and self-review
checklists inside the templates, and in its walkthrough as optional steps. The current README
also pairs Implement with a **converge** command, which checks progress; implement and converge
repeat until converge reports `Converged`. The command syntax has changed across versions
(`/specify`, then `/speckit.specify`, now `/speckit-specify` in the README), so this report
names the phases, not the commands. The official `github/spec-kit` README is the authority on
its current behavior.

polytropos runs the same loop under different names. It splits the loop across two skills and
adds a fifth step that Spec Kit does not have. This report maps each phase, then names where
polytropos goes further and where it does less. Every polytropos claim below names the file
that makes it true. The long form of the argument is `docs/SPEC-DRIVEN.md`.

## At a glance

| Spec Kit | polytropos | Where it lives | Who runs it |
|---|---|---|---|
| constitution | the repo's `CLAUDE.md` invariants, plus each kit's `GUARDRAILS.md` | the target repo; `.claude/kits/<slug>/GUARDRAILS.md` | written by people (repo) and by the architect (kit) |
| **Specify** | the spec half of `PLAN.md`: goal, checkable "done", constraints, out-of-scope fence, with an approval pause | `skills/architect/SKILL.md` Steps 0–1 | `/polytropos:architect`, frontier tier, once |
| clarify | scoping questions before the frontier run; assumptions and open questions listed under the spec draft | `skills/architect/SKILL.md` Steps 0–1 | the architect, with the user |
| **Plan** | the design half of `PLAN.md`: decisions with rationale, risks with tripwires, optional `autonomy:`, `budget:`, `roles:` and `workflow:` lines | `skills/architect/SKILL.md` Step 1 | the architect, after approval |
| **Tasks** | `TASKS.md`: one block per task with a pinned `model`, a self-contained brief, acceptance, a verify command and `evidence:` | `skills/architect/SKILL.md` Step 2; `bin/kit_contract.py` | the architect writes it; `kit_contract.py graph` validates it |
| analyze | structural graph check before the run; drift review at each phase end | `bin/kit_contract.py graph`; the kit's reviewer agent | execute |
| **Implement** | per-task dispatch to the pinned tier, orchestrator-run verify, fresh-context verifier, phase reviewer, one retry, then a frontier consult | `skills/execute/SKILL.md`; `bin/claude_execute.py` and its peers | `/polytropos:execute` on cheaper tiers |
| converge | the loop ends when `bin/kit_contract.py graph` reports every task `done`; each task already converged through its own verify, verifier and retry | `bin/kit_contract.py`; `skills/execute/SKILL.md` | execute |
| *(none)* | **Measure**: a ledger in `NOTES.md` and a scorecard that grades the tiers, the review roles and the spec | `skills/execute/references/ledger.md`; `bin/routing_scorecard.py` | execute writes it; the next architect reads it |

<!-- page -->

## 1 · Specify

**Spec Kit.** The specify phase captures what to build and why: user stories, scenarios, edge
cases and measurable outcomes, deliberately free of implementation detail.

**polytropos.** `PLAN.md` opens with the spec, under the heading the architect skill gives it:
"what and why, no design yet". It holds two sections: the **goal** with a "done" that is
"checkable, not vibes", and the **constraints** with an explicit **out-of-scope** fence that says
what executors must not do.

Then comes the **approval pause**. The architect drafts those two sections, shows them, and
stops. It writes nothing into `.claude/kits/<slug>/` until the user approves the draft in the
conversation. The skill gives the reason: "A misread requirement caught here costs one exchange;
caught after the kit is written, it costs the whole Fable run." The approved text is the spec. If
the design later shows the spec cannot hold, the architect brings the conflict back to the user
instead of quietly rewriting it. The pause is skipped only when the user explicitly says to plan
straight through, and then the handoff says so.

In dispatch mode a subagent cannot ask the user anything, so the run takes two hops. The first
hop explores and returns only the spec draft, the main session relays it and collects approval,
and the second hop writes the kit.

**The difference.** Spec Kit's spec is product-shaped (stories and scenarios). polytropos's spec
is change-shaped: one goal, one checkable done, and a fence. The fence matters more than it
looks, because it is what the executors and reviewers enforce later.

## 2 · Plan

**Spec Kit.** The plan phase records the technical approach and checks it against the
constitution, producing supporting research, data-model, contract and quickstart artifacts.

**polytropos.** Once the spec is approved, the rest of `PLAN.md` is the design:

- **Architecture and key decisions, each with rationale.** The skill's reason: "the 'why' is what
  lets a cheaper model make consistent micro-decisions later". The rationale is written for the
  executors, not for the record.
- **Risks and their tripwires**: what an executor should watch for, and what to do when one hits.
- **Run posture, as optional one-line dials.** `autonomy:` (advisory or auto), `budget:` (caps on
  dispatches, escalations and consults), `roles:` (optional review roles beyond the standard
  trio, out of a fixed vocabulary of seven) and `workflow:` (`reviewed`, `extended` or
  `direct`).
- **Grounding**: when the target repo carries a `graphify-out/graph.json`, the architect can
  ground the plan with `bin/graph_ground.py`. The graph is a first map, never the sole evidence
  for a dependency claim.

The constitution's role is split. Always-on rules live in the repo's `CLAUDE.md`. Rules that bind
only while one kit runs live in that kit's `GUARDRAILS.md`, which the architect must always
write. `tests/test_guardrails_layout.py` fails the suite for a kit that skips it.

**The difference.** polytropos has no separate research, data-model or quickstart files. The
design and its reasons sit in `PLAN.md`, next to the spec they serve. There is no explicit
"check the plan against the constitution" gate at planning time. The fences are enforced later,
at every phase start and every review.

<!-- page -->

## 3 · Tasks

**Spec Kit.** The tasks phase breaks the plan into work items with stable ids, exact file paths,
parallel markers and story labels.

**polytropos.** `TASKS.md` has one block per task, under `## Phase N` headings:

- `id`, `title`, and `status` (`pending`, `in-progress`, `done` or `blocked`).
- **`model`**: the tier the task runs on. `sonnet` is the default, `opus` is for the genuinely
  hard tasks and `haiku` for trivial mechanical ones. Execute passes it as the dispatch's model,
  overriding the agent's own default. The field is never rewritten at run time.
- **A self-contained brief**, executable "by a model with zero access to this conversation":
  files, conventions, exact interfaces, known gotchas, and the why.
- **Acceptance criteria**, concrete and checkable.
- **A verify command**: a shell command that proves the task done.
- **`evidence:`**: `red-green` by default, meaning the verify must be able to fail before the
  work. `regression` or `precondition` mark tasks where passing beforehand is the point.
- **`depends:` or `independent:`**, read by machine. Independent tasks fan out in parallel. This
  is Spec Kit's parallel marker as an explicit graph.

Before the first dispatch, `bin/kit_contract.py graph` rejects a duplicate id, an unknown or self
dependency, or a cycle, and names the fix for each. Execute will not route around an invalid
plan.

The kit also gets its own agents in `.claude/agents/`: an implementer, a read-only verifier and a
read-only reviewer, each with the project's conventions written into its prompt.

**The difference.** A polytropos task carries its own proof (verify plus evidence) and its own
price (the model pin). A Spec Kit task says what to do. A polytropos task also says how to show it
was done and how much model to spend on it.

## 4 · Implement

**Spec Kit.** The implement phase executes the generated tasks, and converge checks the result;
the two repeat until converge reports `Converged`.

**polytropos.** `/polytropos:execute` runs the kit as an orchestrator on the daily-driver tier.
For each task it:

1. Marks the task `in-progress`, checks the budget dial, and dispatches the brief verbatim to the
   implementer on the task's pinned tier.
2. Runs the verify command **itself**: "the implementer's claim of success is not evidence."
3. Sends non-trivial tasks to a **fresh-context verifier** that re-checks the acceptance criteria
   against the files, on `sonnet` by default and on `haiku` only when every check is mechanical.
4. Enforces the **red-green gate**: a `red-green` task whose verify already passed on the
   pre-task tree is *blocked, not done*.
5. On failure, retries once with the failure output. After a second failure it marks the task
   `blocked` and offers a **frontier consult** that carries only that brief, the evidence and the
   relevant `PLAN.md` excerpts.
6. At each phase end, dispatches an **`opus` reviewer** to check the phase against `PLAN.md` for
   drift, and re-reads the fences from disk before the next phase starts.

The same kit also runs headless. `bin/claude_execute.py`, `bin/copilot_execute.py`,
`bin/codex_execute.py` and `bin/cursor_execute.py` honor the same task contract and the same
budget dial. They run verify commands inside `bin/exec_policy.py` and record every dispatch in
`bin/attempt_ledger.py`.

**The difference.** Spec Kit's implement phase hands the task list to the agent. polytropos
splits that agent into roles on different tiers and never takes the builder's word for it.

<!-- page -->

## 5 · Measure (no Spec Kit equivalent)

Every finished task, dispatch and phase review appends a machine-read line to the kit's
`NOTES.md`: `outcome:`, `agent:`, `reviewer:` and `defect:`. The grammar is in
`skills/execute/references/ledger.md`. `python3 bin/routing_scorecard.py --history` turns those
lines into per-tier pass, retry, escalation and block counts across every kit, per-role findings
against confirmed findings, and a tally of the kinds of brief defect found.

That last tally grades the **spec**. When execute confirms that a brief itself was wrong (a stale
pin, a verify that could never fail, a path nobody specified, acceptance criteria that contradict
each other), it records a `defect:` line instead of widening the task until it passes. The
architect's routing guidance tells the next planner to read those kinds "as evidence about YOUR
OWN briefs", and to consult `--history` when choosing model pins. That closes the loop: the next
Specify and Plan are informed by how well the last ones held.

## Where polytropos does less

- **No cross-artifact consistency pass before the run.** Spec Kit's analyze step checks the
  artifacts against each other first. `kit_contract.py graph` checks only the task graph's
  structure. Semantic drift between `PLAN.md` and `TASKS.md` is caught by the phase reviewer,
  after a phase has run.
- **No product-level spec format.** There are no user-story or scenario templates and no
  requirement ids. The spec is a goal, a done check and a fence, which suits code changes better
  than product features.
- **No planning-time constitution gate.** Fences are enforced during execution and review, not
  checked against the design before tasks are written.
- **Specs per change, not per product.** A kit is one change's spec. Nothing aggregates kits
  into a living product specification.

## Where polytropos goes further

- **A cost dimension in the spec.** Every task names its tier, so frontier judgment is spent
  once, on Specify and Plan, and execution runs cheaper. `/polytropos:route` estimates the cost
  before a run, and `python3 bin/routing_scorecard.py <slug> --session <id>` prices a finished
  kit against an all-frontier counterfactual, both from `data/pricing.json`.
- **Proof built into every task.** Verify commands, the red-green rule and independent review
  are part of the task contract, not a convention.
- **The spec is graded.** The `defect:` ledger measures the planner, not just the builders.
- **Bounded autonomy.** Re-routing is advisory by default. Under `autonomy: auto` it moves only
  upward, one tier, never to the frontier. Budget caps stop a run cleanly and say so.

## Run it

```text
/polytropos:architect <task>                # Specify (approval pause), then Plan and Tasks
/polytropos:execute <slug>                  # Implement, on the pinned tiers
python3 bin/routing_scorecard.py --history  # Measure, across every kit
```
